title: Again Our Earthly Cares We Leave
description: Again Our Earthly Cares We Leave in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 32 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “A Blessing sought”, where the book credits them to Pratt's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-gain our earth-ly cares we leave, And to thy courts re-pair; A-gain, with joy-ful feet we come To meet our Sa-viour here.

lines: Again our earthly cares we leave,
Again, with joyful feet we come
The feeling heart, the melting eye,
And shine upon us from on high,
May we in faith receive thy word,
And in the presence of our Lord
Show us some token of thy love,
And pour thy blessing from above,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
